# A single `print` or `printError` of any length

## Documentation

`print` and `printError` hand the whole `String` to the target's write in ONE call, so the length of that
call is the length of the string: a program may print a line of any size with one `print`. On
`wasm32-wasi` the write is WASI Preview2's `output-stream.blocking-write-and-flush`, which the WIT
contract caps at 4096 bytes per call, so that lane writes a longer string as consecutive calls of at
most 4096 bytes each. Every byte arrives, in order, whatever the length.

The cases below print one line each, built from a repeating unit whose length does not divide 4096 (so a
chunk that is dropped, repeated or reordered changes the output) or, for the two exact-cap cases, a
16-byte unit that does. Lengths: exactly the 4096-byte cap, twice the cap, one chunk and a few bytes
over it, and over 64 KiB. Each stream is pinned separately for the over-cap sizes.

## Tests

<!-- test: stdout-exactly-the-cap -->
```maxon
function main() returns ExitCode
	let unit = "0123456789abcdef"
	var line = ""

	for _ in 0 upto 256 'fill'
		line.append(unit)
	end 'fill'

	print(line)
	print("\n")
	return 0
end 'main'
```
```exitcode
0
```
```stdout

```
